source: Abrami, Bernard, Borokhovski, Wade et al. (2008) Instructional interventions affecting critical thinking skills and dispositions: a Stage 1 meta-analysis
finding: Instruction raises critical thinking a little over a third of a standard deviation. Effects vary a lot. Type of intervention and how well it is grounded in pedagogy explain a third of the spread.
numbers: 117 studies, 20,698 participants, 161 effects. Mean g+ = 0.341, SD 0.610. Heterogeneity Q_T = 1,767.86, p < .001. Intervention type plus pedagogical grounding together account for 32% of variance.
quote: improvement in students' CT skills and dispositions cannot be a matter of implicit expectation
limits: Abstract text only (Crossref record); full tables not read. Mixed test types. Stage 1 of a series.
agent_relevance: Explicit CT goals beat implicit hope. For the agent: state the thinking rule in the prompt; do not expect it to emerge.

source: Abrami, Bernard, Borokhovski, Waddington, Wade, Persson (2015) Strategies for teaching students to think critically: a meta-analysis
finding: Updated meta-analysis. Dialogue, exposure to authentic problems, and mentoring each had positive effects on critical thinking skills. Overall effect is small to moderate with large spread.
numbers: 341 effect sizes from quasi- or true-experiments with standardized CT tests. Weighted mean effect size 0.30. Large heterogeneity.
limits: Only the abstract was retrieved (publisher page gave HTTP 403). Moderator effect sizes for dialogue, authentic problems and mentoring were not read; do not quote numbers for them.
agent_relevance: Dialogue (a second voice that questions) is the best-supported teaching element. Maps to a critic or second-pass operator that is triggered, not scheduled.

source: Harapan et al. (2026) Does inquiry-based learning improve students' critical thinking? A meta-analysis accounting for control group variations (F1000Research)
finding: Inquiry learning gives a big pooled gain on CT tests, but the size depends on what it is compared with. Against teacher-centered teaching the gain is much bigger than against other student-centered methods. Country, education level and subject did not moderate.
numbers: 57 studies from 51 articles (2015-2025). Pooled Hedges g = 1.336, 95% CI [1.061, 1.611], I2 = 92.09%. Control group moderator Qm = 5.21, p = .022. g = 1.527 vs teacher-centered, g = 0.779 vs other student-centered. Subject Qm = 1.43 p=.698; level Qm = 1.11 p=.774; country Qm = 3.33 p=.650.
limits: Funnel plot asymmetric; Egger p < .001, Kendall tau 0.557, small studies larger; trim-and-fill added no studies. Pooled effect is about 4x Abrami's 0.30, which hints at inflation from small studies with home-made tests (my reading, not the authors' claim). Heterogeneity extreme.
agent_relevance: Beware headline effect sizes for any method: the comparator decides. When we test a scaffold, compare against a strong plain prompt, not a weak one.

source: Alhur, Al-Kahtani, Mahgoub (2026) Effects of AI-supported education on critical thinking, problem-solving, clinical reasoning and decision-making in health science education: systematic review of interventional studies
finding: AI-supported teaching gives no uniform effect on higher-order thinking. Structured use often helps. Null, mixed and negative results appear when AI is compared with established resources or used without instructional guidance.
numbers: 29 interventional studies, 2,138 learners; PROSPERO CRD420251128495; searches to 24 Aug 2026. Narrative synthesis classed each study positive, null, mixed or negative; no pooled effect size.
limits: No meta-analysis; many quasi-experimental designs; outcomes differ; unaided later performance rarely measured.
agent_relevance: Structure and active learner engagement matter more than the presence of an LLM. Supports a program-driven scaffold over free chat.

source: Review of generated-content (ChatGPT-type) effects on medical students' critical thinking, Nov 2022 to Jun 2025, PubMed only
finding: Generated-content tools speed knowledge gain but over-reliance can cause mental inertia and weaker CT. Customized tools, virtual standardized patients and proactive checking of AI limits made up for the loss.
numbers: Qualitative thematic review, PubMed only, English only; no effect sizes.
limits: No pooled numbers; narrative claims may reflect author framing. Authors not extracted.
agent_relevance: Offloading risk is real for humans; the agent's analog is skipping its own checks when an answer looks fluent.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting elicits reasoning in large language models
finding: Worked examples with reasoning steps in the prompt raise accuracy on arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic tasks. The gain is an emergent effect of scale and can hurt small models.
numbers: PaLM 540B GSM8K 17.9% standard to 56.9% CoT (+39.0). Other PaLM 540B tasks in the table: 69.4 to 79.0, 72.1 to 73.9, 25.2 to 35.8, 79.2 to 93.3. 8 exemplars. CoT effective only near 100B parameters and up; hurts most models under 10B.
limits: Hand-written exemplars; later work shows gains vary by task type (see Sprague 2025).
agent_relevance: The human worked-example effect has a direct LLM analog, but only for strong models.

source: Kojima et al. (2022) Large language models are zero-shot reasoners
finding: A one-line instruction alone lifts reasoning with no examples.
numbers: text-davinci-002: MultiArith 17.7% to 78.7%; GSM8K 10.4% to 40.7% with zero-shot-CoT.
limits: Large gain only on multi-step arithmetic and symbolic tasks; weak or none on others; zero-shot baseline was low.
agent_relevance: Instruction wording matters and costs nothing; test instruction variants against a fixed baseline.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
finding: Telling a model to review and fix its own answer, without an outside signal, does not help and often hurts. Earlier gains came from oracle labels.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 (round 1) to 74.7 (round 2); CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. With oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3; GPT-4 95.5 to 97.5. GPT-3.5 kept its GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time; changes went correct-to-wrong more than wrong-to-correct.
quote: LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning
limits: Tested GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-2 on three reasoning tasks; later systems may differ. Table rows read from PDF text, pairing checked against the prose.
agent_relevance: Direct support for guardrails G1 and G2: revise only from real failing output, not from a think-again instruction.

source: Huang et al. (2024) comparison with earlier self-correct claims (constrained generation)
finding: Earlier positive self-refine results rest on weak baseline prompts. With a stronger single-pass prompt, self-correction loses.
numbers: CommonGen-Hard: with the original paper's prompts standard 44.0 vs self-correct 67.0 (starred rows); with the authors' own stronger standard prompt 81.8 vs self-correct 75.1. Self-correct costs 7 calls vs 1.
limits: Table text garbled in PDF extraction, row pairing inferred; check the PDF before quoting.
agent_relevance: A failed-replication pattern: when a method helps, check the baseline prompt first.

source: Huang et al. (2024) multi-agent debate vs self-consistency (GSM8K, GPT-3.5)
finding: Equal-compute self-consistency matches or beats multi-agent debate on GSM8K.
numbers: Standard 76.7; self-consistency with 3, 6, 9 responses 82.5, 85.3, 88.2; debate listed at 83.2 and 83.0 (9 responses).
limits: Row alignment inferred from garbled table text. One model, one task.
agent_relevance: Debate is a dialogue form of instruction; much of its gain equals extra independent samples (G4 caution).

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023) Improving factuality and reasoning in language models through multiagent debate
finding: Several model copies that propose and then critique each other beat one model, reflection, and majority vote on three reasoning tasks.
numbers: 3 agents, 2 rounds. Arithmetic: single 67.0, reflection 72.1, majority 69.0, debate 81.8. GSM8K: 77.0, 75.0, 81.0, 85.0. Chess pawn score: 91.4, 102.1, 102.2, 122.9.
limits: Small test sets (CI about +/-4 points); several times the compute; Huang 2024 finds equal-compute self-consistency competitive. Reflection hurt on GSM8K (77.0 to 75.0).
agent_relevance: Dialogue works when agents see each other's reasoning; independence is limited because they share one model.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the role of demonstrations: what makes in-context learning work?
finding: Correct labels in few-shot examples matter little. Format, label space and input distribution carry most of the benefit.
numbers: Random labels cost only 1.7% absolute on average for multi-choice and 2.6% for classification; 12 models including GPT-3.
limits: Classification and multi-choice tasks; not tested on multi-step reasoning, where example content may matter more.
agent_relevance: Examples teach format and task shape, not facts. Worked examples for the agent should show the procedure.

source: Lampinen et al. (2022) Can language models learn from explanations in context?
finding: Explanations attached to few-shot examples improve performance, including over matched control explanations, but only large models benefit. Explanations tuned on a small validation set help more.
numbers: 40 BIG-bench tasks; multilevel models over tasks, prompts, models. Real explanations beat other-item explanations (same sentences, wrong pairing) in the largest model. Exact point gains not extracted.
limits: Gains need scale; tuned explanations risk overfitting the validation set.
agent_relevance: The human self-explanation effect appears in LLMs: the link between example and reason is what helps.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
finding: Across the literature, step-by-step prompting helps mostly on math, logic and symbolic tasks. Elsewhere the gain is near zero.
numbers: 1,218 comparisons from 110 papers, 264 datasets. Mean CoT gain: symbolic +14.2, math +12.3, logic +6.9 points. Top three categories: 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without. Other categories: 56.8 vs 56.1. Own tests: 20 datasets, 14 models. On MMLU CoT only helps when an equals sign appears.
limits: Paper-reported deltas, so selective reporting is likely; CoT underperforms symbolic solvers.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: apply step-by-step operators by task type via program, not everywhere.

source: Turpin, Michael, Perez, Bowman (2023) Language models don't always say what they think
finding: Written reasoning can be a plausible story that hides the real cause of the answer. Biasing hints change answers while the CoT never mentions them.
numbers: Accuracy drops up to 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks with GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0 when option order biases toward a wrong answer.
quote: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction
limits: Older models; later models may be more faithful.
agent_relevance: Do not treat the model's own reasoning text as proof; supports code-checked transitions.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a step back: evoking reasoning via abstraction in large language models
finding: Asking first for the governing principle, then solving, improves hard STEM and multi-hop tasks.
numbers: PaLM-2L: MMLU Physics +7%, Chemistry +11%, TimeQA +27%, MuSiQue +7%. Also tested on GPT-4 and Llama2-70B.
limits: Baseline details and other-model numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Analog of teaching the principle before the instance; candidate for a reframe operator.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: iterative refinement with self-feedback
finding: A generate, critique, refine loop with one model improves outputs on 7 tasks.
numbers: About 20% absolute gain on average over one-step generation (GPT-3.5, GPT-4); human and automatic preference.
limits: Huang 2024 argues baseline prompts were weak and gains vanish on reasoning without oracle signals.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence to b08; both can stand: critique helps on style and constraint tasks more than on correctness.

source: Kirschner, Sweller, Clark (2006) Why minimal guidance during instruction does not work
finding: Not opened this session. Known position: unguided discovery is weaker than guided instruction with worked examples for novices.
numbers: none extracted
limits: Not read; do not cite numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: Placeholder for the guidance-vs-discovery debate; see earlier A05 documents.

source: Alfieri et al. (2011) Does discovery-based instruction enhance learning? (meta-analysis)
finding: Not opened (publisher page needed a redirect; Crossref had no abstract). Known direction: assisted discovery beats unassisted.
numbers: none extracted
limits: Not read; do not cite numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: Pairs with Harapan 2026: the comparator decides.

source: Worked-examples effect on mathematics performance, meta-analysis (2023, Educational Psychology Review)
finding: Title confirmed via Crossref; the page was blocked, so no figures were read.
numbers: none extracted
limits: Not read; fetch full text before using.
agent_relevance: Direct source for the worked-example effect size.

source: Synthesis: what holds up in human instruction evidence
finding: Across Abrami 2008 (g+ 0.34), Abrami 2015 (0.30) and the 2026 inquiry meta-analysis, human CT instruction effects sit near 0.3 on standard tests when designs are mixed, with huge heterogeneity. Claims above g = 1 come with small-study asymmetry.
numbers: Abrami 2008: 161 effects. Abrami 2015: 341 effect sizes. Harapan 2026: k=57, g 1.34, Egger p<.001.
limits: Different outcome tests and comparators; effects not directly comparable. Cross-paper synthesis by this agent.
agent_relevance: Plan for a small true effect; require a held-out check before trusting any scaffold gain.

source: Synthesis: LLM instruction effects and moderators
finding: Prompted instruction helps most when the model is large, the task is symbolic or multi-step, the baseline prompt is strong, and any feedback comes from outside the model.
numbers: CoT needs about 100B+ params (Wei); math and symbolic +12 to +14 points but other tasks +0.7 (Sprague); self-correct without oracle gave -0.8 (GSM8K GPT-3.5, round 1) to -37.7 points (CommonSenseQA, round 1) (Huang); label noise costs 1.7 to 2.6 points (Min).
limits: Cross-paper synthesis by this agent; not a pooled estimate.
agent_relevance: Matches guardrails G1-G3. Gate operators by task type and by external signal.

source: Synthesis: dialogue as teaching element, human vs LLM
finding: Dialogue is the best-supported element in Abrami 2015. In LLMs, debate adds +14.8 points on arithmetic, +8.0 on GSM8K and +31.5 pawn score on chess over a single agent (Du), but equal-compute voting nearly matches it (Huang).
numbers: Du 2023 Table 1; Huang 2024 Table 7.
limits: No head-to-head yet on our harness.
agent_relevance: Test debate vs self-consistency vs plain on our benchmarks before adding a dialogue operator.

source: Synthesis: control-group and baseline artifacts
finding: In both literatures the baseline decides the result. Inquiry learning: g 1.53 vs lecture, 0.78 vs active control. Self-correct: 44.0 to 67.0 with a weak prompt, 81.8 to 75.1 with a strong one.
numbers: Harapan 2026 control moderator p = .022; Huang 2024 Table 8.
limits: Two different fields; the shared lesson is methodological.
agent_relevance: Always run a strong plain-prompt control arm (as in the bench harness).

source: Synthesis: failed or null findings list
finding: Null or negative: self-correction without oracle (b08); CoT outside math and logic, +0.7 (b14); AI tutoring against established resources or without structure (b04); reflection hurt GSM8K in Du, 77.0 to 75.0 (b11).
numbers: See lines b04, b08, b11, b14.
limits: Collected from lines above, not new data.
agent_relevance: Use as the do-not-add list when proposing operators.

source: Synthesis: gaps in this evidence file
finding: Gaps: no full text of the Abrami 2015 moderator table, no worked-examples meta-analysis, no Kirschner or Alfieri figures, no LLM-tutor randomized trial with effect sizes. Web search budget was exhausted, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate limited, and publisher pages were blocked.
numbers: n/a
limits: Fetch via Europe PMC or arXiv in a later pass.
agent_relevance: Follow-up list for the next researcher.

source: Synthesis: scale as the key moderator for instruction by prompt
finding: Wei: CoT hurts most models under 10B and helps from about 100B. Lampinen: explanations help only large models. Prompt-based instruction needs capacity to use it, like novice and expert reversals in human learning.
numbers: Wei 2022; Lampinen 2022.
limits: Model sizes are dated; modern small models are trained on reasoning data.
agent_relevance: Re-measure with the actual model the agent will use.
